findings.title: Countries that share a dialing code resolve to whichever comes first in the list, not the user's own country.
findings.body: `findCountryByPhonePrefix` sorts only by prefix length, and the sort is stable, so ties keep their original list order. Several countries share a dialing code: `+1` covers the US, Canada and other NANP countries, and `+7` covers Russia and Kazakhstan. Trigger: a US user comes back to Basic Info with `previousFormData.mobileNumber = '+1555…'`. If the API's country list puts Canada (or any other `+1` country) before the United States, which is likely when the list is alphabetical, `PhoneField` infers Canada. That result takes priority over `fallbackCountry`, so the field shows the wrong flag and the selector opens with the wrong country already selected. It can also apply that country's template and placeholder. I couldn't see the order or the prefix format of the real `useRampsCountries` data, so this depends on it. Fix: when several countries match with the same longest prefix, prefer the fallback country (the user region) if it is one of them. For example, pass `fallbackCountry` into the helper and return it first when its prefix digits match.
